title: Brightwater Mill Lane flood options
brief: I'm the clerk of Brightwater Parish Council and I need an options page on stopping the flooding of Mill Lane, for the councillors who will read it printed before the meeting on 2026-11-10. Under "The problem": the lane floods when the Brightwater Brook rises above 1.9 meters, which happened 4 times last winter, cutting off 63 homes for a total of 9 days. Under "Three options", as a table: A, raise the lane by 0.6 meters, 380000 dollars, 14 weeks of work, 3000 a year to maintain, with the risk that water is pushed onto the 11 homes below; B, a retention pond upstream on the Hale Farm field, 520000 dollars, 30 weeks, 6500 a year, with the risk that the landowner withdraws or the permit takes longer than 20 weeks; C, a pump station and drain, 210000 dollars, 9 weeks, 14000 a year for power and servicing, with the risk that a pump fails in the one storm it is needed. Under "If it fails", what would have to be undone: A, the raised lane stays but the homes below need flood protection of about 90000; B, the pond can be filled back in for about 60000 but the land stays with the council; C, the pumps can be sold for about 30 percent of cost. Under "Recommendation": B, because it protects the whole village and not only the lane, provided the landowner signs by 2026-12-15; if not, fall back to A. Make the recommendation and the fallback easy to find.

edit.request: Change option C's cost to 185000 dollars and its yearly running cost to 11000, and move the landowner deadline to 2027-01-15.
